title: Prove sharp integer inertia for two-facet downsets (no new κ)
body:
## Summary

Scoped mathematical proof with finite exact corroboration: every downset with at most two maximal members and a nonempty member has a nonsingular, symmetric, nonnegative integer disjointness-supported matrix with exactly the largest-star number of nonnegative eigenvalues. This settles the two-facet case of Ellis–Filmus–Friedgut's Conjecture I, recorded as C070 in David Ganz's [PR2849](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/2849). Credit those predecessors and the classical Boolean zeta/Sylvester tools; the construction and proof here were produced by Nick Petalas.

```text
D = 2^(C union A) union 2^(C union B), a=|A| >= b=|B|
within either exclusive cube: ordinary disjointness entries
cross weight: h(0)=1; h(k)=2^k-1 for k>=1
zeta congruence: J_a plus a negative definite Schur complement
inertia = (largest star, remaining sets, 0)
```

The package also gives the exact determinant. The general conjecture remains open; no global literature priority or new kappa is claimed. The [primary paper, section 4](https://arxiv.org/html/2609.28404v1#S4) supplies the conjecture, not an assumed construction.

## Evidence

- **Before:** for two disjoint two-element facets, the ordinary disjointness matrix has inertia (3,4,0), above the largest star size 2.
  **After:** changing the full-facet cross weight from 1 to 3 gives inertia (2,5,0) and determinant -3. Weight 2 has a zero eigenvalue and still three nonnegative eigenvalues.
- The all-size proof uses an explicit Boolean zeta congruence and a diagonal negative Schur complement. The standalone checker independently computes exact rational inertia and determinant for all 49 parameter triples with 1<=a+b+c<=6 and a>=b, including single-cube presentations, up to matrix order 64. It checks every support entry, every star and the integer congruence, with eight enumerated controls.
- CPython 3.12.15, standard library. Both registered commands passed locally in 0.49 s and 0.48 s; package replay passed in 1.19 s. The committed-byte/source-history preflight passed for head 834e5749d0797796af92bdd3031108e5e337fce2 and base ff3cc58e370d0f678e529246f8c73e8094e18fcf. Normal and optimized verifier JSON agree exactly, including source hashes.

Exact reproduction from the repository root:

```sh
/Users/nick/git/integer-mult-bounds/.venv/bin/python3.12 -W error -B research/two-facet-downset-inertia/verify.py
/Users/nick/git/integer-mult-bounds/.venv/bin/python3.12 -W error -O -B research/two-facet-downset-inertia/verify.py
/Users/nick/git/integer-mult-bounds/.venv/bin/python3.12 -B scripts/research_package.py --package research/two-facet-downset-inertia
/Users/nick/git/integer-mult-bounds/.venv/bin/python3.12 -B scripts/check_research_commit.py --package research/two-facet-downset-inertia --check-source-history
```

Any CPython 3.12 may replace the local interpreter path. Expected markers: `PASS_TWO_FACET_DOWNSET_INERTIA`, `PASS_REGISTERED_RESEARCH_PACKAGE`, and `PASS_RESEARCH_COMMIT_BYTES`. The verifier writes no files; its JSON receipt is generated from package hashes.

## Limitations

This is a scoped written proof, not a proof-kernel formalization or a multiplication theorem. Independent human and formal proof-kernel review are unclaimed. No Lean, Docker, selected cold replay, physical supplier, precision/storage implementation or supplier admission was run. The selected frontier is unchanged. Atlas source bytes are pinned as the originating question; the proof and direct verifier have no mathematical/runtime dependency on atlas code or the external paper.

## Open next questions

Can three maximal sets admit the same sharp integer certificate? First write the zeta cross blocks for three disjoint two-element facets. The missing step is simultaneous control of three Schur interactions; the present two-facet negative complement does not supply it.

## Related open work

No matching open PR on the two-facet downset inertia quantity appeared in the targeted live/cached searches. The overlap cache covered 311 open PRs and 4,483 Discussion records; sparse notes and unpublished work remain coverage limits.

The completion refresh read the titles and bodies of all eight other open account PRs created since the [CLAIM](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/discussions/1166#discussioncomment-19147073): #5245 studies Hermitian qubit repair, #5246 F4 Hermitian hyperplane intersections, #5248 symplectic partial-spread completion, #5249 P112 diagonal-completion rank, #5250 matrix-pencil determinant images, #5251 a uniform projective design, #5252 finite etale tensor determinant images and #5253 characteristic-two odd-type fitting rank. None studies the two-facet downset inertia quantity or supplies a competing value for this certificate. Several share atlas provenance, with distinct objects and objectives. No additional computations were run to validate or compare those results.
